summary: The rename dialog renders Field focus and Save focus identically, so a user cannot see that typing is ignored while Save has focus.

When writing the revocation ledger fails, logout returns 500 but the viewer's Sign out handler neither catches nor shows the error, and the in-memory revocation then sends the user to the login screen with no way to retry.
The revocation deadline uses the current session_ttl, so after a restart with a shorter TTL, a cookie for the same viewer that was renewed under the old longer TTL can outlive the revocation.
Logout with an expired but correctly signed cookie skips revocation, so a renewed cookie for the same viewer, minted just before expiry and delivered late or held elsewhere, stays valid.
Claimed race: a renewal that pauses between its revocation check and minting could produce a cookie that expires after the logout's revocation deadline.

A session/new that is admitted but then fails or times out in the new readiness wait leaves its id in `sessions`, so unanswered_refusal() suppresses the recorded refusal and `mj acp` exits 0 although no session/new succeeded.
wait_for_session_start can treat a session as ready before its ACP harness has opened, because the activity classifier ignores acp_ready.

A cross-agent import treats any SessionStarted{resumed:true} as finished replay, but a source adapter that supports session/resume and not session/load is resumed without replay, so the import completes with an empty transcript and the primary starts fresh with no history.
ReviewDispatch::launch validates each request's required hypothesis and then throws it away, so the specialist never sees the risk it was launched to investigate.

Moving spawn_config_rename onto spawn_critical_async puts the post-rename Controller::load reload under the 15 s SAVE_ACK_TIMEOUT, so a slow reload is reported as an unacknowledged save even though the rename succeeded, and the fresh config is dropped.

The new RecoverFailed dialog prints the full recorded error with no bound or scrolling, so a long error (or a short terminal) clips the explanation and the button row, while Enter still runs the hidden focused Recover button.

WorkerRootOwner::acquire creates the worker root owner-only only when it is missing, but the controller always creates the root first with mkdir -p under the normal umask, so on the normal provisioning path the new root stays 0755 and the commit's worker-root hardening does nothing.
The new close-failure recovery dialog is never shown because the close error path only sets a notice, and the removed `x` key was the only other way to force-destroy.
Accumulating streamed chunks runs truncate_text, which collapses and trims whitespace, so a space at the end of an intermediate chunk is lost and the next chunk's word runs into the previous one.
Wrapped profile choices can overflow the fixed-height, non-scrolling resume picker at 80 columns.
Deleting embedded_npm_recipes_match_the_runtime_pins removes the only check that the embedded Codex/Claude package.json files match the runtime pins.
Deleting a_harness_restart_gates_dispatch_until_the_session_is_configured_again removes the only test that HarnessRestarting closes the dispatch gate and SessionConfigured reopens it.
Deleting daemon_restart_without_a_baseline_does_not_hide_pending_work removes the only test that a relay restart does not create a fresh review baseline.
The new 2-second wait for the review-baseline startup step may flake on a loaded runner.
In inline mode the slash-command autocomplete popover is drawn from the top of the viewport and covers the new queued-steer chip row.

When a session relaunches, the stage is merged into its existing per-session home, so a model-catalog (a directory of per-provider files) that the user has since removed or pruned stays in the session.

muse_data_dir compares the profile home to the user's own Muse home by path text, so a symlinked or otherwise aliased path to ~/.config/muse is treated as a separate home and its XDG-data catalog is not found.

The owned-server title prefix check auto-approves a non-owned DSH MCP server whose name is an owned name plus `__suffix`, because `mcp  mj-agents  other  tool` passes the prefix and the leading-space check.
Concurrent model setups share one `<file>.part` path, so one worker can rename another's still-incomplete download into the cache, where a non-empty partial file is then treated as installed.
The ignored end-to-end dictation test still reads `<model dir>/test_wavs`, which the new per-file installer never creates, so the test fails on a fresh cache.
The setup status is shown only in the input block's border title, so on narrow terminals the long per-file message is clipped before the percentage and the `Ctrl-R stop` hint.
A prompt submitted while a config update is in flight is dropped with only a Warning, leaving the UI stuck in Streaming with no PromptDone.
refresh_config_picker keeps the picker selection by numeric index, so a ConfigOptionUpdate that reorders or removes options can retarget the open picker to a different option or value.
The picker modal height (rows+4) leaves room for borders and the 2-row header but not the 1-row footer, so the list gets one row fewer than intended.

On SshBare and AwsEc2 targets the controller records the dispatcher command as a relative path while the worker compares it against its absolute root, so the owned review dispatcher is never preapproved.

On a timeout (or any other panic) in native_muse_turn, the live ACP adapter and the native Muse process keep running while unwinding removes the caller's temporary profile, which holds the copied auth.json.

When the review host never sees the idle view between a prompt-driven turn and a self-started turn, the prompt-driven watch is overwritten by a non-prompt Running view, and the final Running->Idle edge no longer arms the automatic review.

If the idle observation arrives while a deferred recovery copy still holds the gate, the coordinator ignores it, and the later abandon_attempt only clears last_attempted_turn without re-evaluating it. A quiet idle session then gets no recovery copy until some unrelated view change.
Recovery and parked sub-agent wake compare the image worker's bytes with the host worker and copy the host binary over the image link, though both carry the same build.
The ignored Docker integration test assumes agent-dev:latest has no worker, which stops being true once this change publishes :latest with a worker.
build-agent-dev-image.sh only warns when worker inputs are dirty, so the image's worker carries the clean commit's identity.
A dangling symlink at /opt/mjolnir/mj-worker makes `[ -e ]` false, so the probe reports 'absent' instead of an unusable worker.
After a worker reconnect, apply_worker_summary replaces the summarized unread count but keeps unread_agent_message_sequences, so messages counted from live events are counted twice.
Summary hydration counts unread messages for the selected session even while it is visible on the dashboard, which the event path deliberately avoids.

If a chat is opened while the first summary poll is in flight, the pending checkout drops the summary, and the full bootstrap that follows is never passed to recovery, so recovery never sees an already completed turn.
On phones, tabbing from an empty editor to Attach removes composer-has-intent, which hides the action row that holds the button now taking focus.
The finding says the history loader hides #earlier-messages through `hidden`, and the new display:block overrides that.
The finding says the old 25dvh outer limit on #conversation-side still applies on phones and creates nested scroll areas with the new 40dvh inner scroller.
same_installation now calls std::fs::canonicalize, and the Settings screen runs it on the TUI event loop when profile detection results arrive.
When canonicalization fails, the lexical fallback collapses `..` across an existing symlink, so two different homes can compare equal and a real discovered installation is suppressed.
The lexical fallback does not resolve symlinks in the existing prefix, so a missing home reached through an alias still does not match its real path and a duplicate profile is added.
Expanding `~` for comparison suppresses the absolute-path profile, while other consumers use the configured `~` home literally.
The new metadata-only scan in named_like sets preview to None, so sessions that match only by title or project lose the preview text the Archived tab shows as a fallback.

After a turn-review form is answered, any event page applied before the worker records the resolution makes surface_reviewer_elicitations reopen the same form, and nothing closes the stale dialog later.

Calling poll_turn_review_role after each answer starts a second self-rescheduling poll loop for a role that is already being polled, so every answer permanently adds another loop until the review finishes.

SessionStarted reaches the launch registry through the orchestrator and the outer task's loop, but an acp::run error is recorded directly from the runtime task, so an agent that starts and then exits quickly can be recorded as Failed even though its session started.
begin() evicts the oldest launch record even when it is still Starting, so after 64 newer launches an active launch's outcome is lost and its viewer sees 404 and then a timeout.
The viewer's launch watcher does not recheck that it still owns the launch after its awaits, so it can navigate after the card is dismissed or replaced.
The full-width minimized Sessions title shows 'Attention: N' without the most urgent level's glyph, while the compact and tiny forms include it.
attention_level returns Unreachable before checking for a failed review or failed findings handoff, so a session with both ranks and badges as '?' instead of the higher Failed level.
In narrow layout the Sessions rows render minimized but the title badge is filtered on the configured pane size, so the attention summary is missing.
Legacy Row positions are treated as full-history indexes, but an older build that saved while its prefix was still loading wrote a tail-relative index, so the upgraded view restores the wrong entry.
A failed initial sync clears transcript_loading while the session keeps retrying, so the next draw resolves a pending Restoring position to Bottom with empty entries and the saved position is lost.

When the first lease fails because the worker is unreachable, the session actor stays unleased for the whole worker restart, so prompts (or another lifecycle operation) can reach the restarted worker before the checkpoint latches.

adopt_restarted_checkpoint_relay treats any lease failure, including 'session already has a lifecycle operation', as permission to continue on a standalone connection, bypassing the actor's exclusive lease.
worker_connect_needs_restart treats any proxy EOF as a dead worker, so a transient SSH/proxy disconnect makes an ordinary or recovery checkpoint kill a healthy worker and its active prompt.
A broken pipe while writing the hello request is not classified as a dead worker, so Stop still fails without restarting when the proxy exits before the write.
A history-search result that arrives during a clipboard read bumps input_generation and makes the paste be discarded.

The summary's last-agent-message query takes only the newest SQL-qualifying item (LIMIT 1) and returns no preview if that item renders blank, instead of searching earlier messages as the full projection does.

The unread-ordinal SQL uses SQLite's one-argument trim, which removes only spaces, so agent items with only newline or tab text count as unread after restart while is_nonempty_agent_message excludes them.

The startup summary carries an unread count computed from the viewed cursor captured when the task was spawned, and applying it overwrites a count that set_state already recomputed against a newer cursor.
The summary apply accepts an equal applied_event_ordinal, so a summary arriving after a full projection for the same ordinal overwrites the full projection's derived fields.

The summary loader runs the metadata query and the transcript queries as separate autocommit reads, so a concurrent projection save between them yields a summary that mixes an old frontier with newer messages.
The user-message query requires a stable_id starting with 'user:' or 'user-', which would skip user items with other IDs.
delete_empty_workspace allows deleting the 'default' workspace when it is empty, after which every session_contexts insert that relies on DEFAULT 'default' is rejected by the new trigger.
Adding a fourth column to session_contexts breaks existing tests that insert three positional values after migration.
The version-13 migration test resets user_version to 12 on a current database, so the new version-14 migration runs CREATE TABLE workspaces again and fails.
assign_new_session_workspace treats every 'default' session as unassigned, so it can move an existing default-workspace session despite the doc comment saying existing contexts are immutable.
assign_new_session_workspace reads the current workspace and updates it in separate autocommit statements, so two concurrent assignments could both succeed.
The wrapped quota label now asks for its full wrapped height as a Length constraint with no upper bound, so on a narrow and short terminal it competes with the chat input for space.

The pinned field title is drawn as an unwrapped one-row paragraph, so a title wider than the pane (or one with a newline) is clipped and the rest, including ' (required)', can no longer be reached by scrolling.
With a two-row form body, the new allocation gives the request message zero rows, where it previously got one.
The 500 for a stopped capacity poller tells the caller to look up reference `capacity-poller` in the daemon log, but the warning logged on that path never includes that reference.

Every error from resolve_local_repository, including Git failing to run or the checkout being unreadable, is now marked as a precondition refusal, so the caller gets a 409 saying to configure a network remote instead of a 500 with a log reference.
When the right-aligned activity spinner overlaps a chip at narrow widths, the spinner is drawn over the chip, but the chip's full hitbox is still registered.
When a model or effort chip does not fully fit, its clipped part is still drawn in chip styling but gets no hitbox, so clicking the visible chip does nothing.

Chip hitboxes from the prompt border are still checked in component_handles_mouse while the config picker is open, so where the picker covers them, a press on non-control picker body text is claimed by a component instead of starting text selection.
